precepts.text: In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandments, to seek his God. Verse 2: Hezekiah appointed the priests and Levites to their courses to do the works of God in the temple. Those are the works.
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

precepts.why:
“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

precepts.text: Make no marriages with the nations, for they turn the heart to other gods; instead destroy their altars, break their images, and burn their groves.
precepts.point: This obeyed the law directly: rather than intermarry with the nations, Israel was to destroy their altars and burn their graven images.
precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Make no marriages with the nations, for they turn the heart to other gods.

Instead: “thus shall ye deal with them; ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.”

That is the law Israel obeyed directly when the feast was finished. They “went out to the cities of Judah, and brake the images in pieces, and cut down the groves, and threw down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, in Ephraim also and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all.” Then every man returned “to his possession, into their own cities”, the reformation now reaching beyond the temple into the whole land.

precepts.text: Truly tithe all the increase year by year, and do not forsake the Levite within your gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with you.
precepts.point: They lay the tithe in heaps from the third to the seventh month, and when Hezekiah and the princes see the heaps they bless the Lord and his people Israel.
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.” The tithe of “thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks” was brought “that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always.” And the charge ends: “the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.”

Hezekiah restored exactly that. He appointed the priests and Levites “after their courses, every man according to his service”, set “the king’s portion of his substance” for the morning and evening, sabbath, new moon and feast offerings, “as it is written in the law of the Lord”, and “commanded the people that dwelt in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of the Lord.” The Levite was not forsaken.

“And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly.” They laid it by heaps from the third month to the seventh, “And when Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord, and his people Israel.”

precepts.text: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily as to the Lord and not unto men.
precepts.point: This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.
precepts.why:
“And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men”. That is Hezekiah: “in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.”

This is the charge on every one of us. Do the work with everything you have, as unto the Lord, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.

precepts.text: Be strong, show thyself a man, and keep the charge of the Lord to walk in his ways, that thou mayest prosper in all thou doest.
precepts.point: This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.
precepts.why:
David charged Solomon: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself”.

Keeping the charge is what brings the prospering. Hezekiah “wrought that which was good and right and truth before the Lord his God”, sought his God “in the law, and in the commandments”, “and prospered.”

So it is for us: keep his laws and do the work with all your heart, or it will not be blessed.

points: When the feast is finished, all Israel present goes out to the cities and breaks the images, cuts down the groves, and throws down the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh.
Then every man returns to his own possession and city, the reformation now reaching beyond the temple into the whole land.
This obeyed the law directly: rather than intermarry with the nations, Israel was to destroy their altars and burn their graven images.

Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses for burnt offerings, peace offerings, and thanksgiving, and sets the king's portion for the daily, Sabbath, new moon, and feast offerings as written in the law.

He commands the people in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and Levites so they may be encouraged in the law, and the people bring in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, oil, honey, and the tithe of all things.
They lay the tithe in heaps from the third to the seventh month, and when Hezekiah and the princes see the heaps they bless the Lord and his people Israel.

Hezekiah questions the priests about the heaps, and Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answers that since the people began bringing offerings they have had enough to eat with plenty left, for the Lord has blessed his people.

Hezekiah commands chambers prepared in the house of the Lord, and appoints faithful Levites over the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things to distribute the oblations to their brethren by courses, to great and small alike.
The portions are given by genealogy to the priests and Levites and to their little ones, wives, sons, and daughters, for they sanctified themselves in holiness.
Hezekiah does throughout all Judah that which is good and right and true before the Lord his God.
This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.
In every work he begins in the service of the house of God, in the law, and in the commandments to seek his God, he does it with all his heart and prospers.
